parsed.summary: The Lean theorem states Wilson's theorem: for every prime p, the factorial (p-1)! cast into ZMod p equals -1, i.e. (p-1)! ≡ -1 (mod p). This matches the paper exactly. The ℕ subtraction p - 1 cannot truncate, because p ≥ 2 for a prime.

lean_claims.plain: For every natural number p with p prime (supplied as the instance Fact p.Prime), the natural number (p-1)!, cast into ZMod p, equals -1. Equivalently, (p-1)! ≡ -1 (mod p).

paper_claims.plain: If p is a prime, then (p-1)! ≡ -1 (mod p).

coverage.why: Congruence mod p is the same as equality in ZMod p. The hypothesis is exactly that p is prime. The factorial is computed in ℕ and then cast.

lint_verdicts.why: Fact p.Prime gives p ≥ 2, so p - 1 in ℕ is the true predecessor and no truncation occurs.
